title: indigo_mount_ioptron: a position readback failure during motion can end a successful GoTo in ALERT
description: ioptron_read_position() failing once while the mount is slewing publishes ALERT after BUSY, which is then kept, so a GoTo that completes correctly ends as ALERT. Found while working on ticket 42b85be0-1f19-4607-b3c3-746e60317d17 (closed, commit a09e0f878), which introduced the kept coordinates ALERT in indigo_update_coordinates(): an ALERT published after a BUSY stays until the next BUSY. Reproduce in the driver's simulator suite before changing code.

outcome.summary: Pass. Reviewed git diff c912611a4..cb66398ae (merge-base..HEAD). Fix (indigo_mount_ioptron.driver:1621-1636, 1653-1658; .c 1684-1721): position_failures counts consecutive failed poll readbacks, reset on a good read and in on_disconnect (driver:1783; connection loss goes through mount_connection_handler -> on_disconnect; init_mount does not reset it, but every session ends through on_disconnect and private data starts zeroed). The end-of-slew branch keeps BUSY only while !coordinates_read && failures <= 2; the 0.5 s BUSY poll retries, so a persistent failure ends ALERT after at most two extra polls (~1 s); failures during the slew count too, so it can end ALERT earlier, never later. Refused GoTo (ALERT in on_change), abort (ALERT + stopping), the not-yet-sent GoTo branch, idle failures, park/home (decided from :GLS flags, park_issued/home_issued guards and deadlines untouched) and hand-controller slews are unaffected; no new path can stay BUSY forever (a failing get_state keeping BUSY is pre-existing). ioptron_read_position() writes values only on success for every protocol, so values stay the last real read and targets (preserve_values) the request; the sync exit (driver:1939) is unchanged and does not touch the counter. Generated .c/.h/_main.c are byte-identical to output of a freshly built indigo_generator from the worktree source; version 69->70 / 0x03000046; git diff --check clean; formatting fine (empty commented branch matches driver:1646 style). README change is only the script record line, matches TEST_SUMMARY.md and 3.0.0.70; MIGRATION_STATUS 144/0 = 141 registered cases + 3 opt-in --tcp, Comment column untouched; nothing outside mount_ioptron, its test and the two record files changed. Tests: both new cases pass on HEAD; on a scratch build of the pre-fix driver ioptron_goto_survives_failed_position_readback FAILS (ALERT published) and the other passes; on a scratch variant whose retry never ends ioptron_goto_ends_alert_when_position_readback_keeps_failing

Pass (re-review of cb66398ae..a7588164a). (1) mount_ioptron_simulator.c:38-44, 116, 663-686, 709-734, 750-752: a reply rule takes an optional 4th field that sets status_override when the rule fires, with the same '-' => 0 mapping as @status. Backward compatible: 2- and 3-field lines parse as before (count is still atoi of the 3rd field, status 0 = no effect), @status/@halt/@close are unchanged, the status field is stored only on the new rule, and replacing or CLEARing a rule drops it. The only 4-field control in the tree is the new one at test_mount_ioptron_simulator.c:1385, and this simulator is used only by this suite. The header comment documents the field. test_mount_ioptron_simulator.c:1383-1390 is now event-driven: the frozen status '2' keeps the GoTo BUSY until the garbled :GEP# is served; the same rule releases the status, so the :GLS# of that poll reports the end of the slew. The outcome no longer depends on when the test thread writes the control (read_control runs at every command and every 100 ms idle tick, and nothing completes before the rule fires). Rebuilt in the worktree: both readback cases pass on HEAD. With the pre-fix driver source (c912611a4) and the new simulator and test (scratch build), ioptron_goto_survives_failed_position_readback FAILS and the other case passes, so the test still detects the defect. (2) Progress line reworded; it is printed when the GoTo leaves BUSY. (3) The POSITION_READ_RETRIES comment is correct now (.driver:36-37). The .c differs only in that comment, and .c/.h/_main.c are byte-identical to output of a freshly built worktree indigo_generator; version stays 70 (0x03000046), which is fine for a comment-only driver change. The README change is only the record line 2026-11-20 20:45 3.0.0.70 mac arm64 simulator 141/141 OK, and TEST_SUMMARY.md has the same line; MIGRATION_STATUS 144/0 unchanged and still right. git diff --check is clean, formatting follows the rules, and nothing outside mount_ioptron, its simulator, its tes

history.text: Building worktree library, generator and ioptron driver

Reproduction (driver v69, unchanged): new simulator test ioptron_goto_survives_failed_position_readback (protocol 3.0, slew status frozen at the target, then one garbled :GEP# reply in the poll whose :GLS# reports the slew ended) failed: ALERT published after BUSY in ioptron_update_mount_state() end-of-slew branch (if (!coordinates_read) -> ALERT, indigo_mount_ioptron.driver line ~1645 before the fix), kept by indigo_update_coordinates() over the following OK. A failed readback while the controller still reports slewing already kept BUSY; the defect is the poll where the slew ends. Fix (v70): PRIVATE_DATA->position_failures counts consecutive failed poll readbacks (reset on a good readback and on disconnect); the end-of-slew branch keeps BUSY with the last read position while position_failures <= POSITION_READ_RETRIES (2), one more failure ends ALERT as before. Idle failures, refused GoTo and abort unchanged. After the fix both new tests pass (the second, ioptron_goto_ends_alert_when_position_readback_keeps_failing, passed before and after: persistent failure ends and stays ALERT, value = last real read, target = request). Recorded run: 2026-11-20 19:22 3.0.0.70 mac arm64 simulator 141/141 OK. MIGRATION_STATUS 142/0 -> 144/0 (incl. 3 opt-in --tcp cases, not run).
Checking generated outputs against the worktree generator
Building the ioptron driver and simulator test binary in the worktree
Running the two new tests against pre-fix and never-ending-retry scratch variants
Review fixes: event-driven readback test, delay evidence on fixed and unfixed driver
Recorded run after review fixes: tools/run_driver_test.py mount_ioptron

Review findings addressed. (1) ioptron_goto_survives_failed_position_readback is now event-driven: the simulator control rule takes an optional last field <digit|-> that sets the status override when the rule fires; the test injects GEP<TAB>+12060000#<TAB>1<TAB>- while the slew status is frozen at 2, so the frozen status is released exactly when the garbled :GEP# is served and the :GLS# of the same poll reports the end of the slew; the GOTO cannot complete before the failed readback. Evidence with a temporary 1 s delay before the control write: fixed driver v70 3/3 PASS (OK, ALERT never published); base driver v69 (c912611a4) 2/2 FAIL (ALERT published, expected 0 got 6). Delay removed. (2) Progress line now 'GOTO ended after the failed readback' printed once the coordinates leave BUSY. (3) POSITION_READ_RETRIES comment states that failures during the slew count too; regenerated, version stays 70. Recorded run: 2026-11-20 20:45 3.0.0.70 mac arm64 simulator 141/141 OK.
Re-review: running the readback tests on HEAD and on the pre-fix driver

Event-driven option: let the simulator apply the status override when the GEP rule fires (e.g. a rule option chaining @status), or check in the events file that the injected GEP was followed by the released GLS of the same poll and re-inject otherwise. (2) The 'after the failed readback' line is printed after the retry poll (wait for polls+1 = two :GLS# after the control), cosmetic. (3) The POSITION_READ_RETRIES comment (driver:36-38) reads as if only polls after the reported end count; failures during the slew also count. Not run: full suite (implementer's recorded 141/141), protocol profiles other than 3.0 for the new path (verified by reading only), the race in (1) was not reproduced empirically.
